'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
****[[March 2025 Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip]]
*****[[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli Defense Minster]] [[Israel Katz]] orders the [[Israel Defense Forces]] to occupy new areas of the [[Gaza Strip]], and threatens to annex sections of Gaza if [[Hamas]] refuses to release all its remaining [[Gaza war hostage crisis|Israeli hostages]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/mar/21/israel-katz-warns-hamas-gaza-annex-war (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[Israel]] intercepts a [[ballistic missile]] that the [[Houthi]]s in [[Yemen]] claim to have fired at the [[Ben Gurion International Airport]] in [[Tel Aviv]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-military-says-it-intercepted-missile-fired-yemen-houthis-claim-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Kursk offensive (2024–present)|Kursk offensive]]
**** A [[pumping station|gas pumping and measuring station]] in [[Kursk Oblast]], [[Russia]], is set on fire after a major explosion occurs. Russia and [[Ukraine]] blame each other for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/blast-shakes-burning-russian-oil-depot-authorities-say-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/blast-shakes-burning-russian-oil-depot-authorities-say-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)]
***An explosion occurs at an [[oil depot]] in [[Krasnodar Krai]], Russia, caused by a fire that has been burning since Tuesday. The fire spreads to another tank and increases to {{cvt|10000|m2}}, injuring two firefighters. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/blast-shakes-burning-russian-oil-depot-authorities-say-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)]
**[[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[German Navy]] reportedly seizes the [[Panama]]nian-flagged [[oil tanker]] ''Eventin'', suspected to be part of the [[Russian shadow fleet]], along with at least {{Euro}}43.3 million ($46 million) worth of cargo, in the [[Baltic Sea]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-seizes-suspected-russian-shadow-fleet-oil-tanker/a-71999181 (DW)] [https://www.thetimes.com/world/europe/article/germany-seizes-oil-tanker-from-russian-shadow-fleet-fg55tr5rr (''The Times'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] retakes the [[Republican Palace, Khartoum|presidential palace]] in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]], after the [[Rapid Support Forces]]' withdrawal. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c5y0w7pjnp2t (BBC)]
*[[Fambita mosque attack]]
**At least 44 people are killed and thirteen others are injured in an attack on a [[mosque]] in {{ill|Fambita|de}}, [[Niger]]. The Ministry of National Defense blames the [[Islamic State – Sahel Province|Islamic State]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-44-killed-niger-jihadist-attack-authorities-say-2025-03-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse]]
**A 19-year-old dies in hospital from his injuries after a canopy collapsed in 2024 at the [[Novi Sad railway station]] in [[Novi Sad]], [[Vojvodina]], [[Serbia]], which killed 15 others. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/19-year-old-dies-in-serbian-hospital-the-latest-death-in-canopy-fall-that-triggered-mass-protests/ (CTV News)]
*According to the [[International Organization of Migration]], a record 8,938 [[human migration|migrant]] deaths were recorded in 2024, over 200 more than 2023, the previous record year. Most deaths are attributed to [[Asia]], the [[Mediterranean Sea migrant smuggling|Mediterranean Sea]], and [[Migrants' African routes|Africa]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/migrant-deaths-reach-record-high-in-2024-iom-says/a-71994593 (DW)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/3/21/migrant-deaths-hit-record-number-in-2024-un-agency-says (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Heathrow Airport]] in [[London]], [[England]], closes for most of the day due to a "significant [[power outage]]" resulting from a fire at an [[Substation|electrical substation]] in nearby [[Hayes, Hillingdon|Hayes]]. At least 1,351 flights are affected by the shutdown, with many diverted to alternative airports or returning to their origin airport. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/heathrow-airport-london-closes-power-outage/ (CBS News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvg5dg4p2l0o (BBC News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/londons-heathrow-airport-closes-day-power-failure-rcna197420 (NBC News)]
*The [[Lewotobi|Lewotobi Laki-Laki]] [[volcano]] erupts, prompting at least 4,700 villagers to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] and causing at least seven outbound flights from [[Ngurah Rai International Airport]] in [[Bali]], [[Indonesia]], to cancel. [https://www.dw.com/en/indonesia-volcano-eruption-forces-thousands-to-evacuate/a-71996999 (DW)]

[https://abc7.com/post/mass-shooting-today-new-mexico-police-investigating-young-park-las-cruces-nm/16067742/ (ABC News)] [https://channel2now.com/2025/03/22/article/news/crime/authorities-seek-publics-help-to-identify-suspect-in-young-park-mass-shooting-in-las-cruces-new-mexico/ (Channel2 NOW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Namibian general election]]
**[[Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah]] is sworn in as the first female [[President of Namibia]], succeeding [[Nangolo Mbumba]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cly8ln5g12wo (BBC)]
*[[2025 Turkish anti-government protests]], [[Arrest of Ekrem İmamoğlu]]
**Tens of thousands of anti-government protesters hold demonstrations in [[Istanbul]], [[İzmir]], [[Ankara]], and several other cities in [[Turkey]] against the government of [[President of Turkey|Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]], following its [[Arrest of Ekrem İmamoğlu|detention]] of over 100 opposition figures and crackdown on [[freedom of assembly|public gatherings]] and [[social media]] content. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-criticises-opposition-leaders-call-streets-over-mayors-detention-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[President of Tunisia|Tunisian president]] [[Kais Saied]] appoints [[Sara Zaafarani]] as the new [[Prime Minister of Tunisia|Prime Minister]]. She succeeds [[Kamel Madouri]], who has been sacked by Saied amid an economic and migration crisis. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tunisian-president-sacks-prime-minister-presidency-says-2025-03-21/ (Reuters)]
